overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by giving non-specific notice and executive session purposes for 13 meetings and by inconsistently following executive session entry procedures, but found no violation on written notice to the Town Manager or the pre-publication statement; the improper contract execution was cured by open-session ratification.

allegations.summary: Meeting notices for 13 meetings allegedly failed to specify the executive session topic, including that the contract under discussion was the Town Manager's.
allegations.key_passage: The Board's notice for each of the thirteen meetings was not sufficiently specific to advise the public of the issues the Board planned to discuss during its executive sessions.

allegations.summary: The chair's verbal statement of the executive session purpose before each vote to enter executive session was allegedly inadequate.
allegations.key_passage: For the same reasons that the meeting notices were deficient, the verbal statement of the executive session purpose during the nine meetings

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the executive session discussions were not proper under Purpose 2 because the Town Manager's contract had not yet expired.
allegations.key_passage: Discussions relating to the negotiation of contract terms for a non-union employee are appropriate for executive session under Purpose 2, regardless of whether the employee's contract has expired or is imminently due to expire.

allegations.summary: Alleged failure to give the Town Manager written notice of executive sessions discussing him under the Purpose 1 notice requirement.
allegations.key_passage: While the Board did not act inappropriately by not giving written notice to the Town Manager that he was subject of discussion at the executive sessions

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to follow required procedures for entering executive session (open session first, stated purpose, roll call vote) at several meetings.
allegations.key_passage: On August 26, September 24 and 30, and October 7, 2010, the Board did not convene in open session first, did not state the purpose for the executive session, and did not take a roll call vote to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: The contract addendum was signed in executive session on November 9, 2010, which the AG found improper; the later open-session ratification cured it.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Board improperly executed the contract addendum during the November 9, 2010 executive session, it acted appropriately by discussing the contract addendum during a properly noticed open meeting ten days later.

allegations.summary: Executive session minutes omitted a list of documents and exhibits used at the meetings, as required by the law (raised by the AG, not the complainant).
allegations.key_passage: the Board's executive session meeting minutes do not satisfy the requirement that minutes include

allegations.summary: Emails among three members before the December 16, 2010 newspaper statement allegedly constituted improper deliberation by a quorum.
allegations.key_passage: we find they did not constitute improper deliberation because statements characterizing past acts for political purposes are not communications on public business within the jurisdiction of the public body.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
Attend an Open Meeting Law training within ninety (90) days of receipt of the letter, conducted by an attorney or organization familiar with the law and approved by the AG's office.
Within thirty (30) days, review the minutes of each of the 13 executive sessions and amend them where appropriate to include a list of documents and other exhibits used.
remedy_passage: We accordingly order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Board that a determination by our office of similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
